extracted.intended_audience: Authors preparing and submitting papers to NeurIPS 2025 (prospective NeurIPS submitters)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and policies for preparing, submitting, rebutting, and finalizing NeurIPS 2025 main-track papers, including formatting, deadlines, dual-submission, OpenReview usage, and discussion/rebuttal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: How do I submit the camera-ready paper? To edit the Camera Ready file and information, go to the OpenReview page for the paper, and select Edit (top right corner) and then 'Camera Ready Version'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the OpenReview interface's Edit → 'Camera Ready Version' to upload/modify camera-ready PDF and metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you need to include a paper checklist? Yes, please refer to the NeurIPS 2025 Style File for instructions for submitting the checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the NeurIPS 2025 style file instructions when including the required checklist; the checklist should also be included in the single PDF file (camera-ready and submissions where applicable). See PaperChecklist guidance and linked blog post for motivation and filling instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix placement and checklist in single PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you include the appendix in the same PDF? Yes, after the acknowledgement and references. You can also include it in the supplementary materials. The checklist should also be included in the single PDF file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If placing appendix inside main PDF, it must come after acknowledgements and references. Alternatively appendices may be placed in supplemental materials; but the checklist must be present in the single PDF submission when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted edits to title, keywords, and abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you edit the title, keywords and the abstract? Yes, as long as they do not substantially differ from the original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor edits are allowed; do not change these fields in ways that substantially alter the submission compared to the blinded submission used for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author list change policy (add/remove not allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you edit the author list? You can reorder the author lists freely, but we will not allow additions nor removal of authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reordering is permitted at the indicated times, but adding or removing authors is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author list change timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes may be made to the author list until the abstract deadline. After that, authors may be reordered before the submission deadline, and if/when your paper is accepted, but we will not allow additions nor removal of authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additions/removals must be completed before the abstract deadline; after that only reordering is allowed up to submission and acceptance stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-authors must have OpenReview accounts and profiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Do my co-authors need to create an OpenReview account? Yes. Before the full paper deadline, every co-author needs to create (or update) an OpenReview profile. The information entered in the profile is used for conflict resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every co-author has an OpenReview profile with accurate emails and affiliations before the full paper deadline. DBLP and prior publications fields may be left empty if unavailable; add email addresses and affiliations under 'Education & Career History'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling authors with no DBLP or non-CS publications
rubrics_metrics.description: I don't have a DBLP page or previous publications, how can I complete my OpenReview profile? It is okay to leave the DBLP and papers empty in this case, but please make sure to add all of your email addresses and add your affiliations under 'Education & Career History'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have publications but no DBLP page, you can import your papers directly into OpenReview. Non-CS publications need not be uploaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract-deadline is firm
rubrics_metrics.description: I missed the abstract submission deadline. Can I still submit a full paper? No. The abstract submission deadline is firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect exceptions for missed abstract deadlines; ensure abstract is submitted by the deadline (full paper may be submitted earlier, but abstract deadline is strict).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I withdraw my submission? Yes, you can withdraw your submission at any point in the reviewing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may withdraw a submission any time before final decisions; follow OpenReview/NeurIPS procedures for withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract submission content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: What exactly should be submitted by the abstract deadline? The abstract of your paper, which can be edited afterwards up until the full paper deadline. You can also submit the full paper if you wish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum, submit an abstract by the abstract deadline; full paper optional at that time. Abstract remains editable until full paper deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required use of NeurIPS LaTeX style (no Word template)
rubrics_metrics.description: I would like to write my paper using Microsoft Word, but I don’t see a template. Can you provide one? No. The Microsoft Word template has been discontinued. Authors must use the NeurIPS 2025 LaTeX style file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare submissions using the official NeurIPS 2025 LaTeX style file; Word is not supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader impacts / societal impact guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Is a 'broader impacts' statement required and must it fit within the page limit? You are not required to include a section titled 'broader impacts' in your paper. However, you should still consider any potential negative societal impacts of your work. You may include a discussion of these potential negative societal impacts anywhere in the paper (in the intro, in the conclusion, as a stand-alone section, in the supplemental material if appropriate, etc.), but this discussion may not exceed the page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you discuss societal impacts, that discussion counts toward the page limit unless placed appropriately in supplemental material where allowed; consult checklist guidance and blog post for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page-limit and material allowed beyond nine pages
rubrics_metrics.description: What material is allowed beyond the nine-page limit? The main body of your paper must be contained in the first nine pages of your submission. Additional pages containing references, checklist, and the optional technical appendices do not count as content pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure substantive content is within the nine-page main body. References, checklist, and optional technical appendices can occupy extra pages beyond nine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on comparisons to recent/online work (contemporaneous-work rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the policy on comparisons to recent work? Papers appearing online after March 1st, 2025 are generally considered concurrent to NeurIPS submissions. Authors are not expected to compare to those.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to arXiv and other online publications; area chairs make nuanced judgments (including how to determine date of publication). Authors need not compare to work posted after the stated cutoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: arXiv treated same as other online publications for contemporaneous-work
rubrics_metrics.description: Are arXiv papers also subject to the policy above? Yes, we do not distinguish arxiv papers and other published (conference & journal) papers, and the Contemporaneous-Work rule applies in the same way. More nuanced judgements, including how to determine the date of publication, should be made by the area chair handling the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume arXiv is exempt; treat as any other online posting relative to March 1 cutoff, unless AC rules otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-submission prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I submit work to NeurIPS that is currently in submission to another archival venue? The NeurIPS policy on dual submissions explicitly prohibits this. You need to withdraw your submission from the other venue before submitting to NeurIPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit the same (archival) work to another venue while it is under review at NeurIPS; withdraw elsewhere prior to NeurIPS submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: No submission to other archival venues while NeurIPS under review
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I submit work to NeurIPS and then later submit the same work to another archival venue while it is still under review at NeurIPS? The NeurIPS policy on dual submissions explicitly prohibits this. You need to withdraw your submission from NeurIPS first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you plan to submit elsewhere, withdraw from NeurIPS before doing so; simultaneous archival submissions are disallowed in both directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview contact & email troubleshooting
rubrics_metrics.description: Why haven't I received any emails about my submission? All emails are sent from noreply@openreview.net. If you are an author and not receiving email, please log into your OpenReview account and make sure that your preferred contact email is up to date. We have heard that some email servers or spam filters are rejecting email from OpenReview. If you suspect this might apply to your email server, we recommend that you use a different email address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check preferred contact email in OpenReview; consider alternate email if corporate/spam filters block OpenReview; contact OpenReview support at info@openreview.net for technical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal visibility timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the rebuttals be shown to the reviewers/ACs immediately? No, the rebuttals will be revealed to the reviewers/ACs at the end of the rebuttal period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and ACs will only see rebuttals after rebuttal window closes; plan accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: No paper or supplementary revisions during rebuttal/discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Can we upload a revision of our paper during the rebuttal/discussion period? No revisions are allowed until the camera-ready stage. Can we upload a revision of the supplementary materials during the rebuttal/discussion period? No. You may revise it for the camera-ready stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to update main paper or supplementary materials during rebuttal/discussion; revisions allowed only at camera-ready if accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal content policy (new results allowed but original submission is basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Can the rebuttal include new results? Yes, however your original submission will serve as the basis for the reviewers' (and ACs') acceptance recommendations. The rebuttals should serve only to clarify the reviewers' and ACs' questions during the discussion period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If including new results in a rebuttal, understand that decisions primarily rest on the original submitted paper; rebuttal is for clarification, not wholesale extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: No anonymous links in author rebuttal (limited exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Can we include an anonymous link in the author rebuttal? No. Do not use links in any part of the response. The only exception is if the reviewers asked for code, in which case you can send an anonymized link to the AC in an Official Comment (make sure all linked files are anonymized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid links in rebuttals; if code is requested, send anonymized link privately to AC via Official Comment and ensure linked files are anonymized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling last-minute reviewer questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers posted last-minute questions, and the reviewer-author discussion has closed. What do we do? Area chairs are fully aware that authors cannot respond to last-minute questions, so they will take that into account. We cannot extend the author-reviewer discussion period, as many authors, reviewers, and ACs have planned their work according to our schedule, and extensions would cause delay and additional burden for all involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect extensions; ACs will consider timing when assessing late questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal length limit and format
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the length limit in the rebuttal phase? We have stopped supporting the global rebuttal option and increased the per-review rebuttal limit to 10,000 characters accordingly. You may use plain text with markdown formatting supported by OpenReview, but you cannot upload any additional files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each per-review rebuttal is limited to 10,000 characters, plain text with supported markdown, and no file uploads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Comment button usage
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the 'Official Comment' button for? The official comment button serves to send messages to specific readers. During the rebuttal phase it will only be possible to use it for sending messages to the AC. During the rebuttal phase, do not use the 'Official Comment' for posting rebuttal text that should be read by the reviewers. Use the 'Rebuttal' buttons for that. During the discussion phase you will be able to use that button for sending messages to either the reviewers or the AC. Make sure the 'readers' of the message are those you intend to read it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Official Comment to message AC during rebuttal; use Rebuttal interface for reviewer-facing responses; during discussion phase Official Comment can reach reviewers or AC — always set intended readers correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX version and page-length variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Using different versions of LaTeX can yield PDFs of different lengths. What should I do? This is documented here. You can use any version of LaTeX, as long as your PDF obeys the page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different LaTeX versions are acceptable; ensure final PDF complies with page limits irrespective of TeX engine used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find general OpenReview help
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions related to OpenReview: Please visit https://openreview.net/faq for general questions related to OpenReview. If you experience any technical issues, please contact the OpenReview support team at info@openreview.net directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For technical or account issues, use OpenReview FAQ or contact support via provided email.
